ip_top_stories.title: German Court Rules Suno's AI Memorized and Reproduced Copyrighted Songs
ip_top_stories.summary: A German court has ruled that Suno's AI music generator memorized and reproduced copyrighted songs, marking a significant legal finding against an AI music platform. The ruling adds to growing international litigation over AI training on protected works.

ip_top_stories.title: Amid legal battles, Suno says it will start watermarking songs
ip_top_stories.summary: Following copyright litigation, AI music generator Suno has announced it will begin watermarking its AI-generated songs. The move comes as the company faces ongoing legal scrutiny over the use of copyrighted music in its training data.

ip_top_stories.title: Meta Seeks To Block Zuckerberg Depo In AI Copyright Cases
ip_top_stories.summary: Meta is seeking to block the deposition of Mark Zuckerberg in ongoing AI copyright cases. The move signals the high-stakes nature of the litigation surrounding Meta's alleged use of copyrighted material to train its AI models.

ip_top_stories.title: Brian Murray Calls for Industrywide Solutions to Issues Around AI Authorship [Metered]
ip_top_stories.summary: HarperCollins CEO Brian Murray has called for industrywide solutions to address the growing challenges around AI authorship and copyright in publishing. The remarks reflect increasing pressure on publishers to collectively respond to AI's impact on the creative industries.

ip_top_stories.title: Online shadow libraries – and why they're being implicated in AI copyright lawsuits
ip_top_stories.summary: Shadow libraries such as LibGen and Z-Library are increasingly being cited in AI copyright lawsuits, with plaintiffs alleging that AI companies used these repositories of unlicensed content to train their models. The article examines the role these platforms play in the broader AI training data debate.

ip_further_links.title: Door Opens for AI-Assisted Music Royalties, but Verifying 'Human Creation' Remains a Challenge
ip_further_links.summary: New developments may allow AI-assisted music to qualify for royalties, but verifying the required human creative contribution poses significant practical and legal challenges.

ip_further_links.title: No news content for AI-training without licences | Hindustan Times
ip_further_links.summary: Publishers and news organisations are pushing back against AI companies using news content for training without obtaining licences, with calls for mandatory licensing frameworks.

ip_further_links.title: Axel Springer Lobbies on AI Copyright Protections
ip_further_links.summary: Media giant Axel Springer is actively lobbying for stronger AI copyright protections, reflecting growing publisher pressure on lawmakers to address unlicensed use of content for AI training.

ip_further_links.title: Who owns what AI makes?
ip_further_links.summary: A broad examination of the unresolved legal and philosophical questions around ownership of AI-generated content, covering key cases and legislative gaps.

ip_further_links.title: Legislation: AI and copyright: Malaysia doesn't need to start over
ip_further_links.summary: Analysis argues that Malaysia can adapt its existing copyright framework to address AI-related challenges rather than building entirely new legislation.

ip_further_links.title: Guest Post — Buying the Middle: Reading the Wiley Emerald Deal from the Global South
ip_further_links.summary: A critical analysis of the Wiley-Emerald publishing deal from a Global South perspective, examining its implications for academic publishing access and licensing.

ip_further_links.title: Sales Up, Profits Down at HarperCollins in Fiscal 2026 [Metered]
ip_further_links.summary: HarperCollins reported a 6% rise in sales for fiscal 2026 but saw profits fall, amid a challenging market environment for book publishers.
